### 1.1. Little stringy bark creek example for figure

```{r}
#| label: little_stringy_bark_creek
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| fig-cap: "Little Stringy Bark Creek (LIS_453) catchment and stream network."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| eval: false

library(sf)

plot_arrows_on_lines <- function(lines_sf, col = "black", lwd = 2, length = 0.1, angle = 90, upstream = TRUE, downstream = TRUE, cex = 0.5) {
  # Ensure input is an sf object
  if (!inherits(lines_sf, "sf")) stop("lines_sf must be an sf object.")
  
  # Loop through each feature
  for (i in 1:nrow(lines_sf)) {
    coords <- sf::st_coordinates(lines_sf[i, ])
    if (nrow(coords) < 2) next  # skip if too short
    n <- nrow(coords)
    
    # Arrow at downstream end
    if (downstream == TRUE) {
      arrows(
        coords[n-1, "X"], coords[n-1, "Y"],
        coords[n, "X"], coords[n, "Y"],
        length = length, angle = angle, col = col, lwd = lwd
      )
    }
    
    # Arrow at upstream end
    if (upstream == TRUE) {
      points(
        coords[1, "X"], coords[1, "Y"],
        col = col, cex = cex, pch = 19
      )
    }
  }
}


# Connect to MW databases:
mwbugs <- RPostgres::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), "mwbugs", host = "localhost", port = 5432, user = "readonly", password = "reachcode_42")
mwstr <- RPostgres::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), "mwstr", host = "localhost", port = 5432, user = "readonly", password = "reachcode_42")

# load stream and subcatchment data:
streams <- sf::st_read(mwstr, query = "SELECT * FROM streams;")
subcs <- sf::st_read(mwstr, query = "SELECT * FROM subcs;")

# # Fix reach LIS_74 (should be sampleable):
streams$sampleable[streams$reach == "LIS_74"] <- 1 # Set LIS_74 to sampleable

# Site to plot:
# For little stringy bark creek: (LIS_453g)
sitecode_or_reach <- "LIS_453g"

# Get the site coordinates from sites table:
sites <- sf::st_read(mwbugs, query = paste0("SELECT * FROM sites WHERE sitecode_v12 IN ('",
                              paste(sitecode_or_reach), "');"))

# take the site-level character identifier
last_char <- substr(sitecode_or_reach,
                    nchar(sitecode_or_reach),nchar(sitecode_or_reach))
# reach code for site
reachi <- ifelse(last_char %in% 0:9, sitecode_or_reach,
                 substr(sitecode_or_reach,1,nchar(sitecode_or_reach)-1))

sitei <- subcs$site[subcs$reach == reachi]

# Calculate the proportion of the reach that is upstream of the site:
ppn_us <- ifelse(last_char %in% 0:9,
                 0, (match(last_char,letters[1:10]) - 1) * 0.1)

# Distance upstream in meters:
m_dus <- ppn_us * subcs$tot_length_m[subcs$site == sitei]

# calculate distance to outlet for site i:
d2oli <-  subcs$d2ol_pp[subcs$site == sitei] + m_dus

# Each site in subcs has a unique site code, which is an integer.
# Each site has the next downstream site integer as a separate column.
# Get all subcatchments upstream of site i:
subcs_ig <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(subcs[,c("site","nextds")], directed = TRUE)

# All upstream subcatchments:
allusi <- subcs$site[igraph::subcomponent(subcs_ig, as.character(sitei), "in")]
allusi_d2ol <- subcs$d2ol_pp[match(allusi,subcs$site)]
full_LIS_catchment <- subcs[substr(subcs$reach, 1, 3) == "LIS" | subcs$site %in% allusi,] # The whole LIS catchment

# Get stream lines for the LIS_453 catchment:
LIS_stream <- streams[streams$site %in% allusi,] # Subset streams for LIS_453 catchment
LIS_subcs <- subcs[subcs$site %in% allusi,] # Subset upstream subcatchments for LIS_453 catchment
LIS_catchment <- sf::st_union(LIS_subcs$geom) # Creates a union of the subcatchments for plotting the whole catchment

### Creating d2ol line for LIS_453
# Subset LIS_453 stream lines outside of the catchment:
LIS_2ol <- streams[substr(streams$reach, 1, 3) == "LIS",]
LIS_2ol <- LIS_2ol[!LIS_2ol$reach %in% LIS_stream$reach,]

# Merge into a single line:
LIS_2ol_u <- LIS_2ol$geom %>%
  sf::st_union() %>%       # dissolve into one geometry (MULTILINESTRING)
  sf::st_line_merge()      # merge connected segments into LINESTRING

LIS_2ol_geos <- geos::as_geos_geometry(LIS_2ol_u) # Convert to GEOS geometry for buffering
# Create a buffer around the d2ol line:
LIS_2ol$buffer <- geos::geos_offset_curve(
  LIS_2ol_geos, distance = -50, params = geos::geos_buffer_params(
    join_style = "round", quad_seg = 8
  )
)
LIS_2ol$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(LIS_2ol$buffer)) # Convert to sf object
st_crs(LIS_2ol$buffer) <- st_crs(LIS_2ol$geom) # Set the CRS to match the original stream lines

### Stream pieces

### Create the upstream sampleable length of the stream line
# Subset LIS_stream to only include sampleable reaches in LSN:
LIS_sampleable <- LIS_stream[substr(LIS_stream$reach, 1, 3) == "LSN" & LIS_stream$sampleable == 1,]
# sitej <- LIS_sampleable$site[!LIS_sampleable$nextds %in% LIS_sampleable$site] # upstream-most point along the sampleable stream
sitej <- LIS_sampleable$hydroid[!LIS_sampleable$hydroid %in% LIS_sampleable$nextdownid] # upstream-most point along the sampleable stream

# Downstream sites from LIS_453:
LIS_stream_ig <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(LIS_stream[,c("hydroid","nextdownid")], directed = TRUE)

# Get all downstream streams:
alldsi <- LIS_stream$site[igraph::subcomponent(LIS_stream_ig, as.character(sitej), mode = "out")]

# Join downstream sites to LIS_sampleable: #  & LIS_stream$site != 62485
LIS_sampleable <- LIS_stream[LIS_stream$site %in% alldsi,] # Subset LIS_sampleable to only include downstream sites
LIS_sampleable_u <- LIS_sampleable$geom %>%
  st_union() %>%       # dissolve into one geometry (MULTILINESTRING)
  st_line_merge()      # merge connected segments into LINESTRING

LIS_sampleable_geos <- geos::as_geos_geometry(LIS_sampleable_u) # Convert to GEOS geometry for buffering
# Create a buffer around the d2ol line:
LIS_sampleable$buffer <- geos::geos_offset_curve(
  LIS_sampleable_geos, distance = 50, params = geos::geos_buffer_params(
    join_style = "round", quad_seg = 8
  )
)

LIS_sampleable$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(LIS_sampleable$buffer)) # Convert to sf object
st_crs(LIS_sampleable$buffer) <- st_crs(LIS_sampleable$geom) # Set the CRS to match the original stream lines

### Create the upstream non-sampleable length of the stream line  & LIS_stream$sampleable == 0
non_sampleable_hydroid <- LIS_stream$hydroid[LIS_stream$reach == "N7P_13"]
# LIS_stream_ns <- LIS_stream[LIS_stream$sampleable == 0,] # Subset LIS_stream to only include non-sampleable reaches in LSN
non_sampleable_allds <- LIS_stream$hydroid[igraph::subcomponent(LIS_stream_ig, as.character(non_sampleable_site), "out")]
LIS_non_sampleable <- LIS_stream[LIS_stream$hydroid %in% non_sampleable_allds  & LIS_stream$sampleable == 0,]

LIS_non_sampleable_u <- LIS_non_sampleable$geom %>%
  st_union() %>%      # dissolve into one geometry (MULTILINESTRING)
  st_line_merge()      # merge connected segments into LINESTRING

LIS_non_sampleable_geos <- geos::as_geos_geometry(LIS_non_sampleable_u) # Convert to GEOS geometry for buffering

# Create a buffer around the d2ol line:
LIS_non_sampleable$buffer <- geos::geos_offset_curve(
  LIS_non_sampleable_geos, distance = 100, params = geos::geos_buffer_params(
    join_style = "round", quad_seg = 8
  )
)

LIS_non_sampleable$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(LIS_non_sampleable$buffer)) # Convert to sf object

st_crs(LIS_non_sampleable$buffer) <- st_crs(LIS_non_sampleable$geom) # Set the CRS to match the original stream lines


### Setting colour scheme

cbbPalette <- c("#000000", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "grey40")

dW_col <- cbbPalette[2] # dW colour
dWs_col <- cbbPalette[7] # dWs colour
dWp_col <- cbbPalette[2] # dWp colour
dL_col <- cbbPalette[1] # dL colour
dLp_col <- cbbPalette[1] # dLp colour
d2ol_col <- cbbPalette[1] # d2ol colour
sampleable_col <- cbbPalette[6] # Sampleable stream colour
non_sampleable_col <- cbbPalette[6] # Non-sampleable stream colour
downstream_col <- cbbPalette[3] # Downstream colour
site_col <- cbbPalette[8] # Site colour
bar_col <- cbbPalette[1] # Scale bar colour
AF_cell_col <- cbbPalette[4] # AF cell colour
EI_cell_col <- cbbPalette[5] # EI cell colour

# Scale bar code:
add_scalebar <- function(catchment, length, units = "m", cex = 0.8) {
  # loc = c(x, y) bottom-left corner of scale bar
  # length = length of scale bar in CRS units
  # height = height of scale bar in CRS units (defaults to length/20)
  
  height <- length / 20
#  if (!inherits(catchment, "sf")) stop("catchment must be an sf object.")
  loc <- c(quantile(st_coordinates(st_geometry(catchment$geom))[,"X"], probs = 0.8),
           quantile(st_coordinates(st_geometry(catchment$geom))[,"Y"], probs = 0))
  
  # Draw rectangle for scale bar
  rect(loc[1], loc[2], loc[1] + length, loc[2] + height, col = bar_col)
  
  # Add text label
  text(loc[1] + length/2, loc[2] - height*1.5, paste(length, units), cex = cex)
}

# Gridcell location (common across all three figures)
gridcell_XY <- c(357600.5, 5817850.4) # Coordinates of the example gridcell

# Site point
site_cex <- 1.5 # Size of the site point

# adjust label sizes:
label_size <- 1 # Size of the labels on the map
```

```{r}
#| label: little_stringy_bark_creek_EI
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| fig-cap: "Little Stringy Bark Creek (LIS_453) catchment and stream network."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| eval: false

##############
### For EI ###
##############

# dW combines non-sampleable, sampleable, and d2ol reaches
dW_sites <- unique(c(LIS_sampleable$site, 
              LIS_non_sampleable$site, 
              LIS_2ol$site))

LIS_dW <- streams[streams$site %in% dW_sites, ] # Combine the dataframes into one

LIS_dW <- LIS_dW$geom %>%
  st_union() %>%       # dissolve into one geometry (MULTILINESTRING)
  st_line_merge()      # merge connected segments into LINESTRING

LIS_dW_geos <- geos::as_geos_geometry(LIS_dW) # Convert to GEOS geometry for buffering

# Create a buffer around the d2ol line:
LIS_dW$buffer <- geos::geos_offset_curve(
  LIS_dW_geos, distance = 50, params = geos::geos_buffer_params(
    join_style = "round", quad_seg = 8
  )
)

LIS_dW$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(LIS_dW$buffer)) # Convert to sf object
st_crs(LIS_dW$buffer) <- st_crs(LIS_dW$geom) # Set the CRS to match the original stream lines

# dWs is the upstream non-sampleable length of the stream line (same as LIS_non_sampleable)
LIS_dWs <- LIS_non_sampleable
LIS_coords <- st_coordinates(LIS_sampleable)
LIS_dWs$buffer <- st_cast(st_line_sample(LIS_dWs$buffer, 
                                         sample = seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 100),
                                         type = "regular"),
                          "LINESTRING") # Ensure it's a LINESTRING
LIS_dWs$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = LIS_dWs$buffer) # Convert to sf object

# Trim the stream length of the most downstream dWs line for better plotting:
# LIS_dWs$buffer <- st_line_sample(LIS_dWs$buffer, sample = seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 100)) # Ensure it's a LINESTRING
# LIS_dWs$buffer <- st_segmentize(LIS_dWs$buffer, dfMaxLength = 100) # Segmentize the line to make it easier to plot

### Plotting EI map ###

# Plot subcatchments from LIS_subcs, with stream lines from LIS_stream:
plot(st_geometry(full_LIS_catchment$geom), main = "Little Stringy Bark Creek (LIS_453)", border = "grey90")
plot(st_geometry(LIS_subcs$geom), add = TRUE, border = "lightgrey", lwd = 1)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_catchment), add = TRUE, border = "grey40", lty = 2)

# Add streams:
plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 1]), add = TRUE, col = sampleable_col, lwd = 2)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 0]), add = TRUE, col = non_sampleable_col, lwd = 2, lty = 3)
# plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 0]), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_2ol$geom), add = TRUE, col = downstream_col, lwd = 2, lty = 1)

# Add lines for labelling:
plot(st_geometry(LIS_2ol$buffer), add = TRUE, col = d2ol_col, lwd = 2, lty = 2) # D2OL
plot(st_geometry(LIS_dW$buffer), add = TRUE, col = dW_col, lwd = 2, lty = 1) # dW
plot(st_geometry(LIS_dWs$buffer), add = TRUE, col = dWs_col, lwd = 2, lty = 1) # dWs
plot_arrows_on_lines(LIS_2ol$buffer, col = d2ol_col) # D2OL arrows
plot_arrows_on_lines(LIS_dW$buffer, col = dW_col) # D2OL arrows
plot_arrows_on_lines(LIS_dWs$buffer, col = dWs_col) # D2OL arrows

# Add point to represent site LIS_453:
site_XY <- which(LIS_coords[,"X"] == max(LIS_coords[,"X"]))
points(LIS_coords[site_XY,"X"], LIS_coords[site_XY,"Y"], 
       bg = site_col, pch = 21, cex = site_cex) # Upstream-most point of sampleable stream

# Add a square to represent a measured gridcell:
points(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2], col = dL_col,
       bg = "grey", pch = 22, cex = 1.5) # Downstream-most point of sampleable stream

# draw a line from point gridcell_XY to the upmost point of the non-sampleable stream:
LIS_non_sampleable_coords <- st_coordinates(LIS_non_sampleable)
ns_site_XY <- which(LIS_non_sampleable_coords[,"X"] == min(LIS_non_sampleable_coords[,"X"]))
#lines(c(gridcell_XY[1], LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"]), 
#      c(gridcell_XY[2], LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"]), col = dL_col, lwd = 2)
arrows(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2], 
       LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"], 
       LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"], 
       length = 0.1, angle = 30, col = dL_col, lwd = 2)

# Add text labels associated with each line:
d2ol_middle <- st_coordinates(LIS_2ol$buffer)[nrow(st_coordinates(LIS_2ol$buffer)) / 2,]
text(d2ol_middle["X"] + 260, d2ol_middle["Y"], 
     labels = "d2ol", col = d2ol_col, cex = label_size)

dW_middle <- st_coordinates(LIS_dW$buffer)[nrow(st_coordinates(LIS_dW$buffer)) / 2,]
text(dW_middle["X"] - 200, dW_middle["Y"], 
     labels = "dW", col = dW_col, cex = label_size)

dWs_middle <- st_coordinates(LIS_dWs$buffer)[nrow(st_coordinates(LIS_dWs$buffer)) / 2,]
text(dWs_middle["X"]-350, dWs_middle["Y"] + 350, 
     labels = "dWs", col = dWs_col, cex = label_size)

# create a label for dL that is half way between gridcell_XY and LIS_non_sampleable_coords
dL_middle <- c((gridcell_XY[1] + LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"]) / 2, 
                (gridcell_XY[2] + LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"]) / 2)
text(dL_middle[1] + 180, dL_middle[2],
     labels = "dL", col = dL_col, cex = label_size)

# Create a label just below the gridcell_XY point:
text(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2] - 180, 
     labels = "Surface", col = dL_col, cex = label_size)

# Add a legend:
legend("topleft", legend = c("Subcatchment boundary of sampling site", "Sampleable stream", "Non-sampleable stream", "Downstream to outlet",  "d2ol", "dW", "dWs", "dL"),
       col = c("grey40", sampleable_col, non_sampleable_col, downstream_col, d2ol_col, dW_col, dWs_col, dL_col), lty = c(2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# Add a scale bar in CRS units:
add_scalebar(catchment = full_LIS_catchment, length = 1000, units = "m")

```

```{r}
#| label: little_stringy_bark_creek_AF_pruned
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| fig-cap: "Little Stringy Bark Creek (LIS_453) catchment and stream network, showing pruned network overland (dL) and in-stream (dW) measures for attenuated forest cover (AF)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| eval: false

# Pruned dWp and dL removes the non-sampleable reaches from the dW and dL lines
# dWp combines sampleable and d2ol reaches
dWp_sites <- unique(c(LIS_sampleable$site,
              LIS_2ol$site))

LIS_dWp <- streams[streams$site %in% dWp_sites, ] # Combine the dataframes into one

LIS_dWp <- LIS_dWp$geom %>%
  st_union() %>%       # dissolve into one geometry (MULTILINESTRING)
  st_line_merge()      # merge connected segments into LINESTRING

LIS_dWp_geos <- geos::as_geos_geometry(LIS_dWp) # Convert to GEOS geometry for buffering

# Create a buffer around the d2ol line:
LIS_dWp$buffer <- geos::geos_offset_curve(
  LIS_dWp_geos, distance = 50, params = geos::geos_buffer_params(
    join_style = "round", quad_seg = 8
  )
)

LIS_dWp$buffer <- st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(LIS_dWp$buffer)) # Convert to sf object
st_crs(LIS_dWp$buffer) <- st_crs(LIS_dWp$geom) # Set the CRS to match the original stream lines


### Plotting AF map ###

# Plot subcatchments from LIS_subcs, with stream lines from LIS_stream:
plot(st_geometry(full_LIS_catchment$geom), main = "Little Stringy Bark Creek (LIS_453)", border = "grey90")
plot(st_geometry(LIS_subcs$geom), add = TRUE, border = "lightgrey", lwd = 1)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_catchment), add = TRUE, border = "grey40", lty = 2)

# Add streams:
plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 1]), add = TRUE, col = sampleable_col, lwd = 2)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 0]), add = TRUE, col = non_sampleable_col, lwd = 2, lty = 3)
# plot(st_geometry(LIS_stream$geom[LIS_stream$sampleable == 0]), add = TRUE, col = cbbPalette[3], lwd = 2, lty = 3)
plot(st_geometry(LIS_2ol$geom), add = TRUE, col = downstream_col, lwd = 2, lty = 1)

# Add lines for labelling:
plot(st_geometry(LIS_2ol$buffer), add = TRUE, col = d2ol_col, lwd = 2, lty = 2) # D2OL
plot(st_geometry(LIS_dWp$buffer), add = TRUE, col = dWp_col, lwd = 2, lty = 1) # dWp
plot_arrows_on_lines(LIS_2ol$buffer, col = d2ol_col) # D2OL arrows
plot_arrows_on_lines(LIS_dWp$buffer, col = dW_col) # D2OL arrows

# Add point to represent site LIS_453:
site_XY <- which(LIS_coords[,"X"] == max(LIS_coords[,"X"]))
points(LIS_coords[site_XY,"X"], LIS_coords[site_XY,"Y"], 
       bg = site_col, pch = 21, cex = site_cex) # Upstream-most point of sampleable stream

# Add a square to represent a measured gridcell:
points(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2], col = dLp_col,
       bg = AF_cell_col, pch = 22, cex = 1.5) # Downstream-most point of sampleable stream

# draw a line from point gridcell_XY to the upmost point of the non-sampleable stream:
LIS_sampleable_coords <- st_coordinates(LIS_sampleable)
ns_site_XY <- which(LIS_sampleable_coords[,"X"] == min(LIS_sampleable_coords[,"X"]))
# lines(c(gridcell_XY[1], LIS_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"]), 
#       c(gridcell_XY[2], LIS_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"]), col = dLp_col, lwd = 2)
arrows(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2], 
       LIS_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"], 
       LIS_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"], 
       length = 0.1, angle = 30, col = dL_col, lwd = 2)

# Add text labels associated with each line:
d2ol_middle <- st_coordinates(LIS_2ol$buffer)[nrow(st_coordinates(LIS_2ol$buffer)) / 2,]
text(d2ol_middle["X"] + 260, d2ol_middle["Y"], 
     labels = "d2ol", col = d2ol_col, cex = label_size)

dWp_middle <- st_coordinates(LIS_dWp$buffer)[nrow(st_coordinates(LIS_dWp$buffer)) / 2,]
text(dWp_middle["X"] - 250, dWp_middle["Y"], 
     labels = "dWp", col = dWp_col, cex = label_size)

# create a label for dL that is half way between gridcell_XY and LIS_non_sampleable_coords
dL_middle <- c((gridcell_XY[1] + LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"X"]) / 2, 
                (gridcell_XY[2] + LIS_non_sampleable_coords[ns_site_XY,"Y"]) / 2)
text(dL_middle[1] + 120, dL_middle[2]+90,
     labels = "dLp", col = dLp_col, cex = label_size)

# Create a label just below the gridcell_XY point:
text(gridcell_XY[1], gridcell_XY[2] - 180, 
     labels = "Surface", col = dLp_col, cex = label_size)

# Add a legend:
legend("topleft", legend = c("Subcatchment boundary of sampling site", "Sampleable stream", "Non-sampleable stream", "Downstream to outlet",  "d2ol", "dWp", "dLp"),
       col = c("grey40", sampleable_col, non_sampleable_col, downstream_col, d2ol_col, dWp_col, dLp_col), lty = c(2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1), lwd = 2, bty = "n")

# Add a scale bar in CRS units:
add_scalebar(catchment = full_LIS_catchment, length = 1000, units = "m")
```

```{r}
#| label: little_stringy_bark_creek_final

#| fig-cap: "Flowpath distances used in the calculation of Effective Imperviousness (EI, in panel A), and Attenuated Forest cover (AF) using the full stream network (in panel B), and the pruned network (panel C), for . For EI, dW is the instream attenuation length using the full stream network, dWs is the instream attenuation length using non-sampleable small streams only, dL is the overland attenuation length using the full stream network, and d2ol is the distance to outlet length from the sampling site. For AF using the full stream network, dW is the instream attenuation length using the full stream network, and dL is the overland attenuation length using the full stream network. For AF using the pruned stream network, dWp is the instream attenuation length using the pruned stream network, and dLp is the overland attenuation length using the pruned stream network. Panel D provides a legend for panels A-C and a table describing each of the flowpath distances." 
#| fig-width: 8 
#| fig-height: 6

source("functions/setup.R")

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)) # Margins for the three maps
source("af_ei_figure/little_stringy_bark_creek_EI.R")
source("af_ei_figure/little_stringy_bark_creek_AF_full.R")
source("af_ei_figure/little_stringy_bark_creek_AF_pruned.R")
source("af_ei_figure/table.R")
```
